scope: One material final-claim review; original principal text retained
verdict: Selected nominal sampled joint acceptance and one same-condition repeat are supported. No wider superiority or causal claim is established.

improvement_demonstrated.scope: Observed threshold gain against contemporary controller10 source; no Pareto, statistical or unique causal superiority claim

mathematical_influence.scope: Historical candidate-local T2 endpoint computation supported initial T2 choice and later local-versus-nonlinear qualifications. Initial T2 plan did not execute; no new standalone analysis or prediction for altered weights is claimed.

annotations.annotation: Some drafts mislabeled recent 0.04375 metrics or reused 0.025 metrics as the 0.05 source. Canonical controller10 reference 0.05 held speed is 0.02193117642997826 m/s; 0.025 is 0.055484372368599294; 0.04375 is 0.033902366934608644. Result-summary applied_values and exact configurations govern the table; original prose is retained.

Historical T0 alone executed controller9. T1/T2/T3 and all new runs executed controller10; T2 has three flexible segments, seven components and six tendons. Roles may share a physical configuration. The latest actual attempt is fresh verification, while latest development was 0.04375; the selected deliverable stays anchored to its original 0.0375 execution.

The model chose only holding_tip_speed_weight. terminal_tip_speed_weight remained 0.1; its upper bound prevents increases but does not prohibit decreases. There was no controller-family selection or physical structural adaptation.

0.0375 improves joint acceptance and holding speed against contemporary 0.05, while its terminal/holding position errors are slightly larger, still within limits. Two matching sampled passes do not establish broad repeatability, variance, robustness, a full acceptance interval, real-time performance or a unique mechanism. Local affine witnesses are not nonlinear certificates; curvature residuals are rad/m.

Original grant, limits, clock and settled calls were preserved. Before/after transport bindings and verified derived-authority rebinding are archived. Initial stop-attempt markers preceded confirmed launcher termination; confirmed sealed-boundary events establish the actual pauses. No valid simulation was replayed to repair feedback or export.

One independent matching fresh execution already passed in Mainline4. The principal next question also asks transfer to T2/T3 and possible structural adaptation; that component remains open. No Mainline5 experiment was launched.

model_authored_mainline5_question: Under the same frozen nominal condition and seed 17, does the accepted speed-weight-only adaptation (holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0375, terminal_tip_speed_weight fixed at its 0.1 upper bound) still attain the three physical acceptance metrics when (a) independently re-executed as a matching repeat, and (b) transferred to the other supported structural templates T2/T3, i.e. is joint reach-and-hold reachable by control-only tuning, or does it require a structural (segment length/section-scale) change?
next_question_in_report: Can the same speed-weight-only adaptation attain joint nominal reach-and-hold on supported T2/T3, or is supported structural adaptation needed?
